column1: # TITLE: aCGH profiling for non-small cell lung cancer cell lines sensitive or resistant to CPL304110 FGFR inhibitor
# SUMMARY: FGFR signalling is one of the most prominent pathways involved in cell growth and development
column2: as well as cancer progression. FGFR1 amplification occurs in approximately 20% of all squamous cell lung carcinomas (SCC) - one of the most common subtypes of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC)
column3: indicating FGFR as a potential target for the new anti-cancer therapies. However
column4: acquired resistance to this type of therapies remains a clinical issue. Here
column5: we investigated the NSCLC cell lines response and potential mechanism of acquired resistance to novel selective FGFR inhibitor CPL304110. We found that despite significant genomic differences between CPL304110-sensitive cell lines
column6: their resistant variants were characterized by upregulated p38 expression/phosphorylation
column7: as well as enhanced expression of genes involved in MAPK signalling. We revealed that p38 inhibition restored sensitivity to CPL304110 in these cells. Moreover
column8: overexpression of this kinase in parental cells led to impaired response to FGFR inhibition
column9: thus confirming that p38 MAPK is a driver of resistance to a novel FGFR inhibitor. Taken together
column10: our results provide an insight into the potential direction for NSCLC targeted therapy.
